w10_P4_002495: A wind-farm maintenance report finishes with one number in kilonewtons. A hoist raises a nacelle part of mass 132 kg. The acceleration given to that part, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 8x between x = 1 and x = 3. The winch must supply the force that gives that part that acceleration, and the report writes that force in kilonewtons. From that record 14 is subtracted as the counterweight allowance, in those same kilonewton units. The result is multiplied by 4 for the 4 hoists on the tower, and a final 23 is subtracted for the standing tare. What number ends the report, in kN?
w10_P4_002496: On a rocket-sled test bench a data curve y = 5x^2 + 7x is recorded, and the controller takes the exact area under it between x = 2 and x = 3. Subtracting 11 from that area gives the sled's speed, in metres per second, as it passes the gate. The sled's mass plate reads 15000 g, and the energy it carries at that speed is the base value. Six sleds are fired in a run, so the run energy is 6 times the base value. From that total 16 J is subtracted for the losses in the rail brake. The summary sheet writes what remains in kilojoules. What does the summary show, in kJ?
w10_P4_002505: A rollercoaster engineer models the launch section with the curve y = 2x^3 + 1x^2. The car's speed, in metres per second, is the slope of that curve at x = 3. The car has a mass of 56 kg, and the energy it carries at that speed is the raw figure. The sensor then subtracts 2 J for the launch-latch loss and a further 11 J for the wheel bearings. Three cars go out in each dispatch, so the dispatch energy is 3 times the corrected single-car figure. What is the dispatch energy, in J?
w10_P4_002506: A depot audit ends with a single energy figure in kilojoules. A skip of mass 52 kg travels along the rail at a speed, in metres per second, worked out as 8 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 1. The energy the moving skip carries is the base amount. To that the auditor adds 30 J already stored in the buffer spring. A train holds 12 skips, so a train carries 12 times the corrected amount, and the depot dispatches 9 such trains. What is the depot figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002508: A quarry report closes with one number in kilonewtons. A skip whose mass plate reads 159000 g is accelerated up the incline. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 4x^2 + 0x between x = 2 and x = 3. The haul rope must supply the force that gives that skip that acceleration, and 3 N of that force is taken up by the guide roller and subtracted. The remainder is written in kilonewtons, after which two corrections are added in those same kilonewton units: 2 for the drum offset and 25 for the standing preload. The quarry pond holds 800 L of water, which is no part of this. What number closes the report, in kN?
w10_P4_002512: A university lab report ends with one number in joules. A puck whose mass plate reads 13000 g slides across an air table at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the table's 8 sensors, taken 2 at a time. The energy the moving puck carries is the starting value, from which the lab subtracts 23 J for residual air drag. Five pucks are launched per trial, so the trial energy is 5 times that corrected single-puck value, and a further 16 J is subtracted for the exit gate. The report covers 2 identical trials. What is the final number, in J?
w10_P4_002513: A ski-lift safety file ends with one figure in kilojoules. Each chair carries a load whose mass plate reads 26000 g. The chair's speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 9x + 20 = 0. The energy one moving load carries is the base value, and the file records that in kilojoules. A span holds 6 chairs, so a span's energy is 6 times the recorded value, and the lift has 12 spans. The engineer then adds 11 in those same kilojoule units as a fixed margin. What figure ends the file, in kJ?
w10_P4_002520: A freight yard summary ends with one number in kilojoules. Each container of mass 37 kg rides on a shuttle whose speed, in metres per second, is 6 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 5. The energy one moving container carries is the base value, and the summary writes that in kilojoules. A shuttle carries 12 containers, a train pulls 4 shuttles, and the yard dispatches 6 trains. The clerk builds the total up from the single container to the whole yard. What is the yard total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002532: A pinball workshop tests a ball whose mass plate reads 8000 g. Its launch speed, in metres per second, equals the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the machine's 11 bumpers, taken 2 at a time. The energy the moving ball carries is the raw reading, from which 3 J is subtracted for plunger friction. Each machine fires 11 balls in a test, so a machine total is 11 times the corrected reading, and the workshop runs 2 machines. The result is finally written in kilojoules. A 4 L tin of cabinet varnish sits on the shelf and has nothing to do with the test. What is the workshop total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002536: A model-boat club adds together the whole numbers k for k running from 1 to 7. That sum is the launch speed, in metres per second, of a boat of mass 8 kg. The energy the moving boat carries is the raw reading. The club adds 7 J stored in the elastic and subtracts 3 J lost in the guide rail. Twelve boats are launched in the regatta, so the regatta energy is 12 times that corrected single-boat figure, and 25 J is then subtracted for the timing beam. A 60 L tank fills the test pool and is not relevant. What is the regatta figure, in J?
w10_P4_002537: A warehouse packs two consignments of 185 and 328 identical crates into equal full bundles, using the largest bundle size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 18000 g is then pushed at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that bundle size. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value. Three trolleys work an aisle, so an aisle's energy is 3 times the base value. The warehouse has 8 aisles, and the company runs 7 identical warehouses. What is the company total, in J?
w10_P4_002540: A dairy loads two batches of 258 and 266 identical churns into equal full pallets, choosing the largest pallet size that divides both counts exactly. A cart whose mass plate reads 40000 g is then rolled at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that pallet size. The energy the moving cart carries is the base value, and with 5 carts on the floor the floor energy is 5 times it. The log writes that total in kilojoules. It then subtracts 6 and then 4, both in those same kilojoule units, for the two meter corrections. What does the log record, in kJ?
w10_P4_002544: A shipyard winch accelerates a block whose mass plate reads 184000 g. The acceleration given to the block, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 3x between x = 0 and x = 1. The winch must supply the force that gives that block that acceleration. Seven blocks are hauled together, so the gang force is 7 times one block's figure, and the log writes that in kilonewtons. Nine gangs work a berth, and the yard has 2 berths. A 500 L ballast tank stands nearby and plays no part. What is the yard total, in kN?
w10_P4_002548: A mine hoist report ends with one number in newtons. A cage whose mass plate reads 199000 g is accelerated up the shaft. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 5x^2 + 6x between x = 0 and x = 3. The rope must supply the force that gives that cage that acceleration, and 3 N of it is absorbed by the shaft guide and subtracted. Five cages share a shaft, so the shaft demand is 5 times the corrected figure. The mine has 9 shafts, and the group operates 12 identical mines. What is the group total, in N?
w10_P4_002553: An engine test cell drives a mass of 116 kg along a rail. The control curve is y = 3x^3 + 4x^2, and the engineer first finds how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 2. Adding 3 to that value gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to the mass. The rail must supply the force that produces that acceleration. Six rails run in a cell and 7 cells run in the building, so the building demand is 6 times the single-rail force and then 7 times that. The cell's air line is charged to 9 bar, which is irrelevant here. What is the building demand, in kN?
w10_P4_002554: A calibration sheet for a shaker table starts from a control number: the smaller root of x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0. From that number the technician subtracts 8, multiplies what remains by 8, and then adds 25. The value that comes out is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, that the table applies to its payload. The payload's mass plate reads 29000 g. The table must exert the force that gives that payload that acceleration. The room is held at 21 degrees Celsius, which does not enter the calculation. What force, in N, does the table exert?
w10_P4_002565: A bottling plant audit ends with one figure in kilojoules. Two runs of 310 and 387 identical bottles are grouped into equal full packs, using the largest pack size that divides both counts exactly. That pack size is multiplied by 9 and then increased by 16, and the result is the speed, in metres per second, of a carrier of mass 52 kg on the line. The energy the moving carrier carries is the base value, which the audit writes in kilojoules. The plant runs 5 identical lines. A 70 L syrup tank feeds the filler and is not involved. What figure ends the audit, in kJ?
w10_P4_002575: A gymnastics rig report ends with one number in kilojoules. A trolley whose mass plate reads 12000 g runs along a beam at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 5x between x = 1 and x = 2. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value, and the report writes that in kilojoules. From the recorded value 26 is subtracted, in those same kilojoule units, as the rig's standing allowance. The hall contains 9 identical rigs, so the hall figure is 9 times the corrected value. What number ends the report, in kJ?
w10_P4_002578: A bobsleigh centre's summary ends with one figure in kilojoules. A sled whose mass plate reads 49000 g leaves the ramp at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the slope of the curve y = 2x^3 - 2x^2 at x = 3. The energy the sled carries at that speed is the base value, which the summary records in kilojoules. Ten sleds run in a session, so the session energy is 10 times the record, and 21 is then added in those same kilojoule units for the start-house machinery. The centre holds 11 identical sessions. What figure ends the summary, in kJ?
w10_P4_002583: A go-kart circuit tests a kart whose mass plate reads 14000 g. Its speed along the straight, in metres per second, is the larger root of x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0. The energy the moving kart carries is the base value. Five karts run in a heat, so a heat's energy is 5 times that base value, and the timing system records the heat total in kilojoules. A meeting comprises 12 heats, so the meeting energy is 12 times the recorded heat figure, and 19 is then added in those same kilojoule units for the paddock equipment. What is the meeting figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002585: A laboratory glider whose mass plate reads 47000 g slides along an air track. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0. The energy the moving glider carries is the raw reading, from which 7 J is subtracted for the launch-catch loss. The display converts what remains to kilojoules, then adds 10 and subtracts 23, both in those same kilojoule units, as the two standing instrument corrections. The bench also holds a 3 L water bath that plays no part. What does the display finally show, in kJ?
w10_P4_002586: A bakery audit ends with one number in kilonewtons. Two orders of 114 and 298 identical trays are grouped into equal full stacks, using the largest stack size that divides both counts exactly. A carriage of mass 13 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that stack size. The drive must supply the force that gives the carriage that acceleration, and 4 N of preload is added to it. Two carriages run per oven, so the oven force is 2 times the loaded figure, which the audit writes in kilonewtons, and the bakery has 3 ovens. The proofing room is held at 28 degrees Celsius, which is irrelevant here. What number ends the audit, in kN?
w10_P4_002590: A ferry ramp test uses a trolley whose mass plate reads 44000 g. Its speed down the ramp, in metres per second, is 5 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 8. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value. The rig then adds 10 J stored in the release spring and a further 6 J stored in the buffer. Ten trolleys are run in the trial, so the trial energy is 10 times that corrected single-trolley figure. The ramp itself is 25 m long, which is not needed. What is the trial energy, in J?
w10_P4_002591: A launcher rig traces the curve y = 3x^2 + 2x and takes the exact area under it between x = 0 and x = 3. Adding 3 to that area gives the muzzle speed, in metres per second, of a projectile of mass 44 kg. The energy the projectile carries at that speed is the base reading. The rig then adds 21 J for the propellant residue and 26 J for the barrel spring, and finally subtracts 26 J absorbed by the recoil damper. The rig frame stands 6 m tall, which does not enter the calculation. What energy, in J, does the rig report?
w10_P4_002594: A press line report closes with one number in newtons. A ram whose mass plate reads 106000 g is driven along its stroke. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the slope of the curve y = 4x^3 + 3x^2 at x = 2. The drive must supply the force that gives that ram that acceleration. Eight rams work a press, so the press force is 8 times one ram's figure, from which 21 N is subtracted for guide friction and a further 26 N for the return spring. The plant runs 12 identical presses. What number closes the report, in N?
